doc.title: Frank Foster — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Arranging and style in the Basie band
title: What makes the Basie band's use of devices distinctive
summary: The signature is Basie's clink, clink, clink and the band's execution and personality.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: It’s a very interesting notion of being musical. Would you say these devices are signatures of the Basie orchestra, or they’re devices available, used by many big bands?
They’re devices that are universally available and used by every band in existence, but --
Are there any things that are particular signatures of Basie?

The particular signature of the Basie band is mostly contained in Basie’s little statement, clink, clink, clink. You know where that came from. But these devices that are universally used have a special impact when used by the Basie -- it seems like the
Basie band uses them with more effect or more impact than anyone else alive. When they’re done by the Basie band, there’s something special about them.
What do you attribute that to? Is that Basie? Is that the arranger’s taste? Is that the band’s practiced execution?

The band’s practiced execution, the band’s personality. When the Basie band says [Foster sings a fragment of climactic melody], you know it’s the Basie band. A thousand bands could do that, but none of them would sound like the Basie band.
A lot of people can slide across the stage on one foot, but there’s only one James Brown doing it.
There are certain things that no one can emulate.
There you go. You just summed it up.
